findings.title: Renderer tests don't cover "every outcome"
findings.description: The slice's Technical Requirements ask for `renderAdoptionFacts` tests covering "every outcome" (`project-documents/user/slices/261-slice.detection-and-adoption-state.md:336`). Task 8T only tests `brownfield`, `adoption-in-progress` and `NOT_EVALUATED`. It has no case for `greenfield`, `already-planned` or `adoption-closed`. Yet Task 8 requires an exhaustive `never` switch, so those branches will have rendering code that no test runs. Add one `it.each` row for each remaining `AdoptionOutcome` kind, asserting that the outcome bullet names it. This is cheap and matches the criterion as written.

findings.title: No test checks how the missing-guide error reaches the CLI and MCP callers
findings.description:
The Functional criterion says: "A guide without the profile or prompt: `cf build` exits non-zero with the `AdoptionError` message; `context_build` returns it as an error" (slice line 333). Three tasks test the error inside core:
- Task 9T: the resolver throws.
- Task 10T: the integrator rethrows.
- Task 12 #12: the pipeline rejects.

No automated test checks what the two callers do with it. The `cf build` side is covered only by manual walkthrough step 4 in Task 15. The `context_build` error result is not checked anywhere: walkthrough step 5 covers only parity and `template_preview`. Task 11 already edits `build.test.ts` and `contextTools.test.ts`, so add one assertion to each:
- the mocked pipeline rejects with `AdoptionError`, so `cf build` exits non-zero through `handleError`
- the same rejection makes `context_build` return an error result containing the message

findings.title: The Task 15C commit would hold only notes and check-offs
findings.description: Task 15 runs checks and the walkthrough, then "Record each step's outcome under this task". It also says "Any defect is fixed in its own commit", so 15C (`docs: record slice 261 verification walkthrough`) is left with nothing but walkthrough notes and checkboxes in the task file. CLAUDE.md says: "Never make a commit that only checks boxes or only adds notes." Remove the 15C marker. Instead, include the recorded outcomes in the last defect-fix commit, or in the next real commit if there are no defects. Separately, 14C is a whole commit for a single README row. Merging Task 14 into the 13C commit would remove one granular marker. That part is optional.

findings.title: No timing or load test for the sub-second detection target
findings.description: The slice restates an NFR: detection adds under one second to a Phase 0 build. There is no `tests/load/` task. D2 deliberately chose to have tests check the walk's caps (`MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`, early exit at the line threshold) rather than timings. The task file's Context Summary explains this and points to the Task 3T cap tests. This is a design decision, not a planning gap, and with no load test there is no CI gating to wire up.

findings.title: `detection/` now imports from `adoption/`
findings.description: In Task 3, `detection/sourceVolume.ts` imports `BROWNFIELD_MIN_SOURCE_LINES` from `adoption/adoptionOutcome.ts`. Tasks 3 and 6 import `AdoptionError` from `adoption/contracts.ts`. So the "facts only" module depends on the "policy" module. The design requires this: D1 puts the threshold in one place, and D2 makes the walk throw `AdoptionError`. Task 7 prevents a runtime cycle by using `import type` for `SourceVolume`. Implementers should know this direction is intended.
